slides.0.title: Grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Merlot, País, Carignan, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
slides.1.title: Reds: Cabernet and Carmenère
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Cabernet Sauvignon
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The largest red variety at over 40,000 ha (Wine With Seth, year not given)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Carmenère
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 10,800 ha, over 95% of the world's Carmenère (Wine With Seth, year not given; Wikipedia's 2009 figure is over 8,800 ha)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Style
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Carmenère has softer tannins than Cabernet Sauvignon and medium body; picked too early it shows aggressive green pepper, too late it turns jammy (Wikipedia)
slides.1.content: Cabernet Sauvignon is the biggest red; Carmenère is Chile's most distinctive signature.
slides.2.title: Other reds and heritage varieties
slides.2.highlights.0.title: País
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Mission grape brought in the colonial era, Chile's oldest variety; old vines have drawn attention recently
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Four big varieties
slides.2.highlights.1.content: SAG 2023: Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, País and Merlot together make up 56% of wine-grape area
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Carignan and others
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The story of old-vine, dry-farmed Carignan is covered in Levels 2 and 3
slides.2.content: Chile's varietal mix has international varieties alongside heritage ones such as País and Carignan.
slides.3.title: Whites and cool-climate varieties
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Sauvignon Blanc
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Chile's largest white variety (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Chardonnay
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Another major white, especially valued from cooler coastal sites
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Pinot Noir
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Benefits from coastal areas cooled by the current and sea breezes; regional detail follows in Level 2
slides.3.content: The success of whites and Pinot Noir mostly comes from the cool coastal areas shaped by the current and sea breezes.
